title: field-lab-console-usability-session-notes-apr2025
participants: 6 participants across three customers: fintech startup (ops lead), health-tech (platform engineer), marketplace (product manager). Sessions were 45–60m remote moderated tests using mid-fidelity wireframes for Routes & Rollouts and a lightweight Metrics panel.
body:
Research goal:
- Validate whether the proposed Routes UI makes it obvious which model variant is serving traffic and how to configure fallbacks.
- Observe where users look for cost/latency per-route breakdowns and how they act on regressions.

Method:
- Moderated remote sessions (Zoom + Figma prototype).
- Tasks: 1) Identify active model variant for a simulated high-cpu route. 2) Configure a canary rollout (10% -> 50%). 3) Inspect a recent latency regression and create a mitigation.
- Think-aloud encouraged; screen-recorded; quick SUS at end.

Prototype notes:
- Wireframes were v0.6: route list + right rail details; rollout modal; small metrics panel (sparkline + last-24h summary).
- Known limitation: no hover state for variant tags; no deep link to rollout history.

Raw observations (verbatim-style snippets):
- "Where do I see which model is actually serving? The variant tag seems decorative." — PM (marketplace)
- "I expected to click the latency number to jump to traces; had to hunt in Observability tab." — Platform engineer (health-tech)
- "The canary slider is nice but I wasn't sure if 10% meant sessions or tokens." — Ops lead (fintech)
- Several participants assumed the right-rail metrics were aggregated across all models unless labeled explicitly.

Behavioral patterns we saw:
- Scan-first: users scan route list columns for name, then variant tag, then latency. Many skip small text under tags.
- Defensive rollback mindset: when shown a regression they immediately look for a \"rollback\" or \"fallback\" action (expectation: one-click revert).
- Cost-first tradeoff: fin/ops asked for per-model cost estimate alongside latency when changing rollouts.

Quantitative markers from sessions:
- Average time to correctly identify active variant: 42s (range 12s–1m45s).
- Success rate for creating a canary rollout (following correct % semantics): 4/6 without facilitator help.
- Mean SUS (quick) score: 68 (small sample, indicative).

Synthesis — key findings (short):
1) Variant visibility is too low-contrast and described with ambiguous labels. Users need stronger affordances (badge + tooltip + click-to-details).
2) Rollout semantics are unclear (percent semantics). We should label units (requests vs tokens) and surface session vs token targeting.
3) Metrics-to-action gap: users expect metric points to be actionable (jump to traces, open rollback, open change history).
4) Cost context matters: decisions to shift traffic require immediate estimated cost delta.

Design implications / recommended changes:
- Variant affordance: convert small text tag into a colored pill with short verb (e.g., "active: v1.3") and an info icon that opens a compact details flyout (model size, quantization, created_at).
- Rollout modal: add explicit unit selector (requests | tokens) with short explanation and a confirm summary that shows estimated cost impact for the next 24h at current traffic levels.
- Metrics panel: make sparkline points clickable. Click opens a small action menu: [Open Traces] [Open Rollback] [Create Incident]. Also add hover tooltips with last-24h % change and sample latency distribution.
- One-click rollback: expose a contextual fallback action on Route row. Require two-step confirmation for safety but make it discoverable (ellipsis menu + contextual undo toast).

Prioritized backlog (suggested):
- P0: Variant pill + flyout (JIRA: UX-1101) — high impact, small surface change.
- P0: Rollout unit selector + confirmation summary (UX-1105) — reduces fatal errors in canary creation.
- P1: Clickable sparkline + action menu (UX-1120) — improves incident response flow.
- P1: Per-rollout cost estimator (hook into pricing service) (ENG-PRC-37) — requires infra support, mid-sized.
- P2: Deep-link to rollout history and metric annotations (UX-1133).

Quick wins observed in session (can be shipped in a week):
- Increase variant tag contrast and change wording from "v1.3 (variant)" to "active: v1.3".
- Add one-line helper copy under rollout slider: "Percent of requests routed to canary (requests by default)."
- Add hover tooltip on latency column: "Click to open traces" placeholder.

Risks & open questions:
- Pricing estimator accuracy — requires agreement on what "estimated cost" uses as baseline traffic. Need PO/finance input.
- Rollout unit semantics — product decision: default to requests or tokens? Need to align with Hosted API docs.
- Accessibility checks: colored pills must have accessible labels and non-color indicators.

Action items (owner / due):
- Alyssa: Draft flyout copy and redlines for variant pill (due 2025-04-22).
- Marco: Spike on cost-estimator wireframe + API feasibility (due 2025-04-29).
- Priya: Add clickable-sparkline prototype in Figma and test with 2 customers (due 2025-05-06).
- Samir: Create JIRA tickets for P0 items (UX-1101, UX-1105) and assign to PM (due 2025-04-18).

Appendix — notable quotes (for marketing / PR):
- "If you can't tell which model is serving in 10 seconds, you don't trust the console." — Product Manager
- "A rollback that takes 2 clicks will save my weekend." — Ops lead

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Run an unmoderated test with the updated tag copy and rollout unit label (A/B) to measure time-to-identify.
- Coordinate with docs to align wording on rollout semantics before dev rollout.

File provenance / context:
- Prototype version: figma.com/file/ExampleProto/console-v0.6
- Session recordings saved in drive: /product/research/session-recordings/apr2025/
- This doc will be attached to PRD (JIRA-PRD-551) as field-data appendix.
quick_findings: Variant visibility ambiguous; rollout percent semantics unclear; users expect metrics to be immediately actionable; cost info required in-rollout flow.
prioritized_backlog: UX-1101 (variant pill + flyout) - P0; UX-1105 (rollout unit selector + summary) - P0; UX-1120 (clickable sparkline) - P1; ENG-PRC-37 (cost estimator) - P1; UX-1133 (rollout history deep-link) - P2.
